newsitem.title: FRANCE: Worms denies signing Athena sale accord.
newsitem.headline: Worms denies signing Athena sale accord.

text.p: French holding company Worms & Cie denied on Wednesday it had signed an agreement on the sale of its Athena insurance subsidiary.
"Worms & Cie formally denies that a protocol agreement has been signed with anyone concerning the future of Athena," the company said in a statement.

Business daily Les Echos earlier reported that Generali of Italy and Worms had signed a protocol agreement on the purchase of Athena by the Italian insurance company, after the Worms and Generali narrowed differences over valuations.
Worms chairman Jean-Philippe Thierry said on February 24 that Athena was worth 13.4 billion francs in a disposal.
Worms' annual shareholder meeting is due on Thursday, when further information is expected.

Les Echos reported that Morgan Stanley had been asked to value Athena. Generali had initially valued the French insurer at nine billion francs, while insurance companies valued it at between 10 and 11 billion francs, the report said.
